solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trialled international edition

parts.note: an international match in cricket or rugby is a Test

explanation.surface: A trial run of an international edition of some publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trialled has been put to the test, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Crime that puzzles us each day?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stealing, a criminal offence
second meaning: the Financial Times, read as two words, whose crossword is set every day

explanation.surface: A wry question: is there some daily wrongdoing that keeps baffling us?
explanation.walkthrough: Split as THE FT, the answer is the newspaper itself, whose crossword puzzles its readers every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a crime, and split in two the word names the Financial Times newspaper.

clue.text: In retrospect, recognise a danger

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the following words, running across their join

parts.note: the letters run from the end of retrospect into the start of recognise

explanation.surface: Looking back on events, someone realises a hazard was there all along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retrospect' tempts you to read backwards, but the letters run forwards across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a looming threat, as in the spectre of war, so it stands for a menace.

clue.text: One using foreign oil expert

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange or alien, so the letters of the words oil expert are rearranged

explanation.surface: An overseas petroleum specialist who takes advantage of others.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploiter takes unfair advantage of people, so someone using others fits.

clue.text: Son clowns about for judge

indicators.note: about means going round, so the clowns surround the son

parts.note: asses are fools or clowns

explanation.surface: A boy fooling around, offered as a way of sizing someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or appraise, a direct synonym of the verb judge.

clue.text: Instigator of Starmer's right-wing plot

indicators.note: an instigator starts things off, so this takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of Starmer's
a Tory is a member of Britain's right-of-centre Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Who started the conservative scheme attributed to Keir Starmer, the UK Labour leader?
explanation.definitionFit: The plot of a novel or film is its storyline, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Take a look at East Ender's tipple

indicators.note: an East Ender is a Cockney Londoner, who drops the initial h, so the drink is said the Cockney way

parts.note: a highball is a long mixed drink, a spirit with soda over ice

explanation.surface: An East London resident pausing to inspect their favourite drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys from London's East End drop their aitches, so highball comes out as 'ighball, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball something is informally to stare at or inspect it closely.

clue.text: Rupert Murdoch guzzling daughter's drink

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so the daughter goes inside the description of Murdoch

parts.note: Murdoch's company owns the Sun newspaper, so he is the Sun owner
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: The media mogul knocking back his daughter's cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid owned by Murdoch's News Corp.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Acknowledgement it's right to hold article back

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is then read in reverse
to hold means the first pair of letters keeps the article inside it

parts.note: 'T is the old contracted form of it, as in 'tis and 'twas
a piece is an article, as in a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone insists it's proper to withhold a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: T and R wrap round PIECE to give TPIECER, and 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is a written acknowledgement that payment or goods have been received.

clue.text: Prominent female ready to accept overseas cash

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the foreign money sits inside the word for ready

parts.note: food that is done is ready
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: A leading woman prepared to take payment in foreign currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or senior woman in a field, so a leading lady.

clue.text: Wine from eastern US? That's unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of eastern US are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A wine from the east coast of America would be a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauternes is a sweet French white from Bordeaux, which is why an American one would be unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet dessert white from Bordeaux, an example of the category.

clue.text: Still writing stuff for the Herald?

indicators.note: a herald proclaims aloud, so the word is as a town crier would speak it

parts.note: stationery is paper, envelopes and pens

explanation.surface: Is there still paper and ink being supplied to the Herald newspaper?
explanation.walkthrough: Herald looks like a newspaper's name; here it is the announcer whose spoken words make the two spellings identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary means not moving, the adjective sense of still.

clue.text: Impatient to find silver and turn back

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: back says the word for a turn is written in reverse

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Someone eager to discover silver, then head home.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, keen to see or hear something.

clue.text: Phrase that is translated

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stock expression of a couple of words
second meaning: the English words 'that is' put into Latin

explanation.surface: A dictionary gloss: a phrase meaning that is, put into another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Id est is the Latin behind the abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is a two-word Latin expression whose English rendering is 'that is'.

clue.text: I suspect British trainee is drunk

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker suspecting a British apprentice has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like the speaker's verb after I, but it is the signal to rearrange B and TRAINEE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective inebriate means intoxicated, a formal word for tipsy.

clue.text: Falling for a belly button adornment?

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach
bling is flashy jewellery, the decoration worn on a navel

explanation.surface: Having a soft spot for a navel piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: A belly button adornment is read as bling for the tum. 'Falling for' looks like infatuation, but 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbling means dropping or toppling over, a synonym of falling.

clue.text: Bootlegged whiskey the stuff of fantasy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: illegally distilled spirit, especially in Prohibition-era America
second meaning: foolish talk or fanciful nonsense

explanation.surface: Is illicit liquor something out of a dream?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both illicitly distilled liquor and silly, unrealistic ideas or nonsense.

clue.text: Hannibal imprisoning ancient city scholar

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking up, so the city goes inside the surname

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the cannibal of The Silence of the Lambs
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: The Carthaginian general Hannibal capturing an old city and its learned man.
explanation.walkthrough: Hannibal suggests the Carthaginian general, but it is the fictional Dr Lecter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer is an academic who teaches at a university, a learned person.

clue.text: Crazy old rocker welcoming cry of pain

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the yelp goes inside the rocker

parts.note: a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth devoted to rock and roll
ouch is what you shout when hurt

explanation.surface: A mad old rock star who lets out a yelp as someone arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Touched is informal for slightly mad, as in touched in the head.

clue.text: More trouble, billions unaccounted for

indicators.note: unaccounted for means missing, so the letter for billions is removed

parts.note: bother is trouble or fuss

explanation.surface: Further financial problems, with billions gone missing from the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean additional or further, as in some other ones, the sense of more.

clue.text: A suspended sentence?

parts.note: a court's sentence is literally suspended when the punishment is death by the rope

explanation.walkthrough: A suspended sentence normally means a punishment deferred; here it is a sentence that leaves someone suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution by the noose is the punishment where the condemned person is literally left suspended.

clue.text: The language of echoing Zulu drums

indicators.note: echoing says the hidden letters are read backwards
of says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The tongue spoken by the beating of African drums.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no signal for the hidden step; 'of' supplies it, the letters being taken out of Zulu drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, an example of a tongue.

clue.text: Criminal, in our view, is without defence

indicators.note: without means outside here, so the view phrase wraps around the defence

parts.note: to us means in our opinion
a reason is a justification or defence offered for an act

explanation.surface: Someone insists that an offender has no excuse whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means lacking on the surface, but in the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasonous means guilty of betraying one's country, a criminal act in law.

clue.text: One American writer, or two?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Mark ..., author of Huckleberry Finn
second meaning: an archaic word for two

explanation.surface: Is there one American author, or a pair of them?
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens, and twain is the old word for a pair.

clue.text: Complete madman losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A total lunatic who has lost his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means total or absolute, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: F for fool

parts.note: the letter F is what tops the word fat, its leading letter, so it is the head of fat

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss: F stands for fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: the head (first letter) of FAT is F, which is the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a stupid person, an informal word for an idiot.

clue.text: Criticise beer served in Olympic venue

indicators.note: served in means the drink is placed inside the venue

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics
a pint is a measure of beer

explanation.surface: Complaining about the beer on offer at the Olympic Games.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip into someone is an idiom for attacking or criticising them fiercely.

clue.text: With head sacked, bank's activity is coming to a close

indicators.note: the head is the first letter, and sacked means dismissed, so it goes

parts.note: lending money is what a bank does

explanation.surface: The bank's business is winding down now its chief has been fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending means finishing or concluding, so it means drawing to a finish.

clue.text: Solicitor having breakfast in pub?

indicators.note: in places the breakfast food inside the drinking place

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an egg is a typical breakfast

explanation.surface: A lawyer eating breakfast at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitor suggests a British lawyer, but it is someone who solicits, asking for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar solicits money from passers-by, so he is literally one who asks for alms.
